Compute Match — Customer Guide (Find,
Request and Track GPU Clusters)
This guide is for customers (also called Offtakers): organizations that want to reserve GPU capacity
from NVIDIA Cloud Providers (NCPs).
Customer menu
Click your name in the top-right to open the account menu:
Menu item Route
Request a Cluster /customer  (redirects to Find a Cluster to
Reserve)
My requests /customer/reservations
Logout —
The header also has Page Help ( ? ), User Manual (book icon), Share Feedback, and the What’s
New bell.
Step 1 — Find a Cluster to Reserve
Route: /customer/reservation-request/available-clusters . This is the customer landing page. It
shows GPU clusters from all NCPs on an interactive world map plus capacity cards.

Each card shows City, GPU count, and Earliest Available Date. Cards are labelled Current
(available capacity) or Future (capacity starting later). An amber note means the cluster already has
pending requests. If the platform admins set a pending-request cap, oversubscribed clusters are
hidden.
Selecting clusters
1. Narrow the list with ﬁlters.
2. Click a map bubble or a card.
3. Optional: turn on Send request to multiple NCP’s (needs the send_request_multiple_provider
scope). Checkboxes appear; you can select up to 3 clusters (conﬁgurable). Selecting more
shows a warning.
4. Click Request a Cluster to open the reservation form with your selection pre-ﬁlled.
Changing the Platform while cards are selected asks you to conﬁrm clearing the selection.
Step 2 — Fill the reservation form
The form opens in a modal with three sections.
Cluster Details
Pre-ﬁlled and read-only when you picked a cluster.
With several clusters, they are shown as Option 1, Option 2… separated by “or”, with an
amber banner: these are alternatives, and your request will be matched with one cluster
based on NCP availability.
For custom requests, GPU Model and Geographical Region are required and Country is
optional.

If you ask for more GPUs or an earlier date than the cluster shows, a yellow warning appears; you
can still submit and negotiate with the NCP.
Form buttons
Submit reservation request validates and submits ( POST /api/v1/reservation-request ). On
success you see “Successfully created Reservation Request” and land on the request detail
page.
Clear Form resets ﬁelds but keeps the cluster pre-ﬁll.
Clicking outside or pressing Esc after typing asks why you are leaving, or asks you to Keep
editing or Discard. The × and Cancel buttons close immediately.
Custom requests (no matching cluster)
If nothing ﬁts, click Submit a custom request (banner under the ﬁlters) or Submit Custom
Request (empty state). Your current ﬁlters are carried over as hints. A custom request is not sent to
a speciﬁc NCP; NVIDIA Platform Admins broker it manually and move it through:
Open →  In Review →  Matched or Unserviceable. You can cancel it while it is Open or In Review.
Custom requests never expire. You get an email at each step.
Step 3 — Track requests in My Requests
Route: /customer/reservations .
Columns: Request ID (shown as “REQ-1 - Status”), Customer, Contact Email, Platform,
Geographical Region, Country, Requested GPUs, Total GPUs, Requested Date, Start/End
Date, Duration (Hours), Status.
Multi-NCP requests show as a grouped row with one child row per NCP.
The date under the status chip is when it moved to In Process, Contracted, Rejected, Expired
or Cancelled. Rejected rows have an info icon with the NCP’s remarks.
Filters: Status, Hosting Provider (hidden for multi-provider), Platform, Geographical Region,
Country, Sort by request date, Clear All.
With no requests you see No requests found with a button to create one.
Step 4 — Reservation detail
Route: /customer/reservations/{reservationId} .
A headline states the status, for example “Your Reservation request is awaiting NCP
acceptance” or “Contract Complete!”, with the expiry date when relevant.
Reservation Summary: organization, contact email, period, GPU count, platform, region,
country, rejection remarks, terms acceptance.
Proposal History: every proposal (yours and NCP counteroffers), grouped by region when
several NCPs are involved.
Cancel: available while Awaiting NCP Acceptance, Awaiting Provider/Customer Approval, In
Process or Expired. Conﬁrm in the modal; you may give a reason. All involved NCPs are
notiﬁed by email.
You cannot accept or reject NCP proposals on this page; the NCP conﬁrms the contract.
What happens after you submit
1. You get a “request received” email.
2. Each selected NCP gets a magic-link email and has 7 days to accept.
3. When an NCP accepts, the request goes In Process and you get an introduction email so you
can negotiate directly. The contract window is 45 days.
4. When an NCP clicks Conﬁrm Contract, your request becomes Contracted; other NCPs on
the same request are cancelled as superseded.
5. If every NCP rejects, the request is Rejected. If all deadlines pass, it is Expired and you get
one consolidated expiry email.
Feedback
After creating a request you may see “How was the Request a Cluster experience?” with 1-5 stars
and Submit Feedback. When cancelling or leaving the marketplace you may be asked why. You
can also click Share Feedback in the header at any time.
